newsitem.title: USA: June S&P 500 rally puts bear trend into question.
newsitem.headline: June S&P 500 rally puts bear trend into question.

text.p: This week's rally in Standard and Poor's 500 futures has left technicians to muse whether it signals an end to the bear trend or just a well-deserved rest in a downward trending market.

June S&Ps crashed through key support levels last week to touch a 4-1/2-month low of 736.70 -- an 11 percent retracement from the February high. But the contract spent this week recovering, posting three consecutive days of sharp gains. On Thursday, June erased earlier gains and closed down 2.20 points at 766.10, after trading in a range from 764.30 to 773.60.

Floor traders pointed to resistance at a two-week high of 774.60 set last week, calling it a "make-or-break" level. If the market fails to move decisively through that level, the downtrend could resume in force, they said.
Others speculated that buy stops rest above there, which could take the market back near record high territory.

"We are in a position to turn the trend back to up and that occurs above 774.60," said Jim Hyerczyk, a commodity trading advisor and technician. He said the market was at a critical juncture for determining the intermediate term trend.
Should the market rally above 774.60, Hyerczyk said June S&Ps must hold above 756.10 on any pullback to verify the uptrend.
"The first break down is where the buying comes in and that's what will secure the trend and make the market move up," he said.
A failure to challenge 774.60 means the intermediate downtrend remains intact for now, he said.
Many agreed the market was in trend-defining territory, while several technicians said this week's price action shows the market is making a bottom.
"I think we are beginning to shut down the break," said Tim Ransford, technician analyst with Dean Witter Reynolds.

The rise through 761.00 signaled a break of tough resistance, Ransford said. "We could probably pull back to that point and be okay," he said , but 764.00 was a key point to gauge the near-term health of the market. Staying above there "tells me the market has more to bounce," he said.
Staying above 764.00 does not necessarily mean a challenge to the all-time high of 827.80, "but we are shutting down the break and beginning to confirm a pullback low of 736.70."
Others said the bear trend was intact.

"Considering that we made a high at 827.80 and went almost straight down to 737.00, for the market to rally from the 737.00 low to here is just a little drop in the bucket," said Jake Bernstein, a technician with MBH Commodities.
"I'm not too excited about it," Bernstein said. "The indicators are still down, the trend is still down, and overall I'm still bearish.
He put resistance at 782.50 with support at 757.00.
Greg Nie, a technician with Everen Securities in Chicago, said the market was likely to settle into a consolidation band after highs are made for this week.

"I think the probabilities favor going into a sideways pattern that will seem like a tight band for this market," Nie said. The expiration of April options could boost the market this week, but once that is over, the market should settle into a range below the expiration-related highs, he said.
